# Independent audit: actual roof patches and eight-node mass exchange



The finite linear-programming argument in Section 1 gives an attained affine upper majorant tight at each sampled radius, including boundary bases. When the entire radius graph is affine, the whole graph is allowed as a face; otherwise its minimal sampled faces are proper upper faces. Projection is injective on each because it lies in the graph of an affine function.

The midpoint-face implication in Section 2 has the correct direction: a face containing a parent contains both source and partner. Consequently a source's minimal face is contained in its parent's minimal face, and every terminating basin and its partners lie in the terminal root's face.

For Section 3, any integer point in a projected face is first a positive-volume base by actual Minkowski interpolation. The finite upper majorant then applies at that integer base, forcing equality of its radius with the interpolated radius and hence membership in the face. This proves the complete projected lattice set, including relative-dimensional faces.

The centroid argument uses the homothetic shape in the required way. Within a face, equal affine radii make every anchored Minkowski inclusion an equal-volume inclusion between full-dimensional convex bodies. It is therefore set equality, so its centroid identity is exact. The terminal root lies in the relative interior of the face and admits a representation using every sampled face point with positive coefficient. Perturbing those coefficients in both directions along an arbitrary affine dependence shows that all centroid data obey that dependence. Thus a single affine centroid map exists on the entire completed patch. Affine radii alone are not being mistaken for global centroid affinity.

The exact face enumeration and revised-profile obstruction in Section 4 agree with the independent note eight-base-upper-face-incidence-and-patch-budget-obstruction.md. The selected patches have Helly numbers two and three, overlap at one graph point, and give maximal independent score \(344/3<469/4\) in the chosen integer mass units.

The Section 5 exchange is a separate valid positive result. The exact graph identities place points 6 and 7 on the same ray from 4 opposite point 2. Every closed containing halfspace therefore captures point 2 or both 6 and 7; equality on the line captures all three. Combining this with the disjoint pair 3,5 and point 4 gives \(B+\min(G,C)\). the contributor and edge radius comparisons give \(w_6,w_7\le w_4\le w_2\), so \(C\le B+G\).

With \(D=\max\{A,G,L,B+\min(G,C)\}\), if \(C\le G\), the total is the sum of \(A,G,L,B+C\), each bounded by \(D\). If \(C>G\), use \(A,L,B+G,C\), with the last bounded by \(B+G\le D\). Hence \(T\le4D\). The corresponding deterministic centers are actual graph points. Ordinary Grünbaum in each counted fiber handles every ambient closed cap, including a zero continuous normal.

For the revised profile, the stronger ray score is \(176\); the earlier score \(172\) from treating 2,6 as a single pair is also valid but weaker. No exact maximal-depth assertion is required.

The general theorem is the face decomposition and affine-centroid patch property. The positive aggregate depth theorem remains restricted to the eight-node incidence pattern. Neither the failed independent patch allocation nor the proved exchange is promoted to a general forest theorem.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
